nodes.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real normed space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be continuous. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ is continuous.
nodes.title: Continuity of the cutoff approximants

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real normed space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be any function. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ takes the value $0$ at $a$.
nodes.title: Cutoff approximants vanish at the left endpoint

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real normed space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be any function. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ takes the value $0$ at $b$.
nodes.title: Cutoff approximants vanish at the right endpoint

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space, let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $p \in [0, \infty]$, and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be continuous with $g_0 \in L^p(\mu)$. Then for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ lies in $L^p(\mu)$.
nodes.title: Cutoff approximants stay in $L^p$

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real normed space, let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and put $\delta_n = (b - a)/(n + 1)$. The $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ is the function $x \mapsto \varphi(x)\, g_0(x)$, where $\varphi$ is the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta_n$.
nodes.title: Cutoff approximants

nodes.summary: Let $a < b$ be real numbers, let $1 \le p < \infty$ and let $E$ be a real normed space. Write $L^p([a, b])$ for $L^p$ with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to $[a, b]$. For every $f : \mathbb{R} \to E$ in $L^p([a, b])$ and every $\varepsilon \in (0, \infty]$, there is a continuous $g : \mathbb{R} \to E$ with $g(a) = g(b) = 0$, $g \in L^p([a, b])$ and $\|f - g\|_{L^p([a, b])} < \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Continuous functions vanishing at the endpoints are dense in $L^p$ of a compact interval

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real normed space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$. If $g_n$ denotes the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$, then $\|g_0(x) - g_n(x)\| \le \|g_0(x)\|$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Pointwise bound on the cutoff error

nodes.summary: For all $a, b, \delta \in \mathbb{R}$, the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is a continuous function $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the vanishing cutoff factor

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\delta > 0$. For every real $x$ with $a + \delta \le x \le b - \delta$, the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ takes the value $1$ at $x$.
nodes.title: The vanishing cutoff factor equals one on its plateau

nodes.summary: For all $a, b, \delta \in \mathbb{R}$, the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ takes the value $0$ at $a$.
nodes.title: The vanishing cutoff factor vanishes at the left endpoint

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $\delta$, the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ takes the value $0$ at $b$.
nodes.title: The vanishing cutoff factor vanishes at the right endpoint

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$, the value at $x$ of the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The vanishing cutoff factor is at most one

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$, the value at $x$ of the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is at least $0$.
nodes.title: The vanishing cutoff factor is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$, the value at $x$ of the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is $\max\bigl(0, \min\bigl(1, \min((x - a)/\delta, (b - x)/\delta)\bigr)\bigr)$, where division by $0$ is read as $0$.
nodes.title: Vanishing cutoff factor

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
